title: OTWONO Content Object
description: What the content store records about one object: the chunks it is made of, how large it is, and how visible it may be. The content_id is derived from the chunk list alone and from nothing else — not the label, not the filename, not who stored it — so two nodes holding the same bytes agree on its name even if they label it differently. That is what lets any holder of a chunk serve any other node (ADR-0015). Chunking parameters are a network-wide constant (ADR-0016) and are recorded here so an object split under other rules can be detected, which is all that can be done about it.

content_id.description: BLAKE3 over the domain separator, the chunking version, the chunk count, and each chunk's digest and length in order. Order is part of the name: the same chunks rearranged are a different object.

chunking.description: The parameters that produced this split, fixed by ADR-0016. A different value means the object's chunks cannot be shared with this node — not that it is corrupt.

chunks.description: In order. An empty array is a zero-length object, which is valid and stores nothing.

size_bytes.description: Must equal the sum of the chunk lengths. Checked before a record is written and again when one is read.

visibility.description: Absent means private, and so does any value not in this list. A reader must never fail on an unrecognised label — it must treat it as private, so that damaging a record cannot make its contents more available (CLAUDE.md Section 8). An object labelled shared MUST carry a sharing envelope: a shared label over plaintext chunks would claim a protection the bytes do not have. The converse does not hold — a demoted object keeps its envelope, because its bytes are still sealed and dropping it would leave the owner unable to read their own object.

metadata.description: Never part of the identity. A media type, an original filename, a service's own key — all things that legitimately differ between two nodes holding the same bytes.

sharing.description: Present when this object's chunks are ciphertext (ADR-0019). A shared object is encrypted as a whole before it is chunked, so its chunk digests and its content_id are over ciphertext: a holder cannot confirm a guess at the plaintext, and the object does not share an id with the same file stored public. The envelope is NOT part of the content_id, so substituting a nonce prefix or a recipient's copy yields an object that still verifies as the right bytes and then fails to open — a denial, never different plaintext.

encryption.description: The plaintext sealed in 1 MiB frames with the STREAM construction, the frames concatenated, and the result chunked. Framed rather than one AEAD call so an object larger than memory can be sealed and opened; STREAM rather than independent frames so truncation and reordering fail to decrypt instead of yielding a plausible shorter object. A value this build does not recognise must be refused, never guessed at.

nonce_prefix.description: Base64, 19 bytes. STREAM spends the remaining five bytes of the 24-byte XChaCha20 nonce on a big-endian frame counter and a last-frame flag. Fresh per object: the same content key with two prefixes produces unrelated ciphertext.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: What the object was before sealing. size_bytes measures the ciphertext, which is larger by 16 bytes per frame.

sealed_keys.description: The per-object content key, sealed once per recipient. This list IS the authorized set — a separate authorized.nodes alongside it would be a second fact that could disagree, and the disagreement would be a security bug whichever way it went. An empty list is not a shared object, it is an object nobody including its owner can open. A recipient appearing twice is refused: there is no way to tell which copy is meant. That this list names who a node shares with is an unsolved leak (OQ-28).

recipient.description: The recipient's NodeID in text form, bound as AEAD additional data so a copy addressed to one node cannot be presented as another's.

ephemeral_public_key.description: Base64 X25519 public key of the sender's per-seal keypair, discarded immediately after sealing. Ephemeral so the sealing node needs no long-term key of its own, and so two seals of one key to one node are unlinkable.

sealed.description: Base64 ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext of the 32-byte content key.
